newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper editorials - Sept 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper editorials - Sept 5.

text.p: - With 299 days left before the British colony reverts to China, the Hong Kong media focussed its comments on the decision of Chief Justice Sir Ti Liang Yang to run for the post of post-colonial Chief Executive.

-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS said Sir Ti Liang Yang showed an unserious attitude by being away from Hong Kong and while somebody else announced the important news that he would run for the post of Chief Executive. It urged Yang to resign from his present post as Chief Justice immediately. It said it was still unknown what was behind his nomination, but it was clear Yang had no clear plans and was adopting a wait-and-see attitude.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL said the reason why Lu Ping, director of the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, changed his stance towards Governor Chris Patten was because wise Chinese leaders did not want to see a political impasse caused by bad relations with a heavyweight British politician. It said if Hong Kong's economic value remained unchanged, China would tolerate the Democrats and let the people Beijing chose rule Hong Kong.

-- MING PAO said that if the Chinese leaders did not act against Japanese occupation of the Diaoyu Islands, China would be in no position to talk about soverignty on the international stage any more. It said the response of China and Taiwan was disappointing. Several billion U.S. dollars worth of Japanese loans could not buy the dignity of the Chinese nation, it said.

-- Enligh-language HONGKONG STANDARD said the Sino-British relationship seemed to be moving into a very practical phase. It said the media must avoid viewing the Sino-British relationship in terms of winners and losers and must encourage progress.
